# enstow

> A secret-aware dotfile manager combining GNU stow symlinking with seamless sops and age decryption.

enstow manages modular dotfile packages across platforms with native symlink tracking and in-memory decryption for secret files (e.g., .age and .sops.yaml). Plaintext secret targets are written with strict permissions (0600) without ever storing plaintext secrets in version control.

## Architecture & Directory Layout

`enstow` is implemented in Rust (2021 edition) as a single static binary. It is structured around modular packages inside a dotfiles repository:

```text
dotfiles/
├── .enstowignore             # Global ignore patterns
├── zsh/
│   ├── .zshrc               # Regular file -> symlinked to ~/.zshrc
│   └── .zshrc.local.age     # Encrypted secret -> decrypted to ~/.zshrc.local (mode 0600)
├── nvim/
│   └── .config/
│       └── nvim/
│           └── init.lua     # Symlinked to ~/.config/nvim/init.lua
└── git/
    └── .gitconfig           # Symlinked to ~/.gitconfig
```

### Repository Layout

- `src/`: Core library and CLI binary implementation.
  - `src/lib.rs`: Library root exposing modules.
  - `src/main.rs`: CLI executable entry point.
  - `src/cli.rs`: Command line parsing using `clap` (derive API) and shell completions generator.
  - `src/stow.rs`: Traversal, file action planning (`FileAction`), symlink operations, collision handling, and status auditing.
  - `src/crypto.rs`: Secret type detection, in-memory decryption (`age` crate and `sops` CLI), encryption, and atomic secure file writes (`0600`).
  - `src/config.rs`: Multi-format configuration loader (TOML, YAML, JSON) with precedence resolution.
  - `src/error.rs`: Domain errors categorized via `thiserror`.
- `tests/`: Integration test suite covering CLI dispatch, stow, unstow, restow, prune, collisions, ignore rules, crypto, status, completions, and configuration.
- `assets/`: UNIX roff manual page (`enstow.1`) and sample configuration file (`config.example.toml`).
- `completions/`: Generated shell completion scripts for Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell, and Elvish.
- `Taskfile.yml`: Task automation definitions for cross-compilation, test coverage, formatting, and linting.

---

## Installation & Prerequisites

### Prerequisites

- **Runtime:**
  - `age` / `rage` (optional CLI; `age` Rust crate is compiled into the binary).
  - `sops` CLI (optional; required only if `.sops.yaml` / `.sops.*` encrypted files are used).
- **Build from Source:**
  - Rust 1.75+ toolchain (`cargo`, `rustc`).

### Installation Methods

#### Homebrew

```bash
brew tap nicholaswilde/tap
brew install nicholaswilde/tap/enstow
```

#### Build Locally

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nicholaswilde/enstow.git
cd enstow
cargo build --release
cp target/release/enstow /usr/local/bin/
```

#### Via Task

```bash
task build:local
```

---

## CLI Usage & Subcommands

```text
enstow [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]
```

When run without a subcommand (`enstow`), it defaults to executing the `apply` command with common arguments.

### Global Options & Common Arguments

#### Global Options

- `-C, --config <PATH>`: Explicit path to configuration file (TOML, YAML, or JSON). Can also be set with `ENSTOW_CONFIG`.
- `--log-level <LEVEL>`: Log level filter (`trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `off`).
- `-v, --verbose`: Verbose output (`-v` for debug, `-vv` for trace). Conflicts with `--quiet`.
- `-q, --quiet`: Quiet output (`-q` for warn, `-qq` for error). Conflicts with `--verbose`.
- `-h, --help`: Print help.
- `-V, --version`: Print version.

#### Common Arguments (shared across `apply`, `restow`, `unstow`, `status`)

- `-s, --source <PATH>`: Source directory containing dotfiles (defaults to `.` or config/env).
- `-t, --target <PATH>`: Target directory where dotfiles are applied (defaults to `$HOME`).
- `-n, --dry-run`: Preview actions without modifying the filesystem.
- `-f, --force`: Overwrite existing files or conflicting symlinks.
- `-b, --backup`: Relocate conflicting files to a backup directory instead of aborting or unlinking.
- `--backup-dir <PATH>`: Destination directory for conflicting files (defaults to `<target>/.enstow-backup`).
- `--prune`: Remove stale symlinks pointing to nonexistent source files within managed packages.
- `--age-key-file <PATH>`: Explicit path to age identity key file (`$ENSTOW_AGE_KEY_FILE` or `$SOPS_AGE_KEY_FILE`).
- `-i, --ignore <PATTERN>`: Additional ignore pattern (can be specified multiple times).
- `[PACKAGES...]`: Specific packages to manage (e.g. `zsh nvim git`). If omitted, all subdirectories or configured packages are processed.

### Subcommands

### apply

Symlinks non-secret files and decrypts secret files into target directories.

```bash
# Apply all packages from ~/dotfiles into $HOME
enstow apply --source ~/dotfiles

# Apply specific packages in dry-run mode
enstow apply --source ~/dotfiles --dry-run zsh nvim

# Apply with automatic backup of conflicts
enstow apply --source ~/dotfiles --backup zsh
```

### restow

Combines pruning stale symlinks/secrets with re-applying packages in a single command. Equivalent to running `enstow unstow` on stale files followed by `enstow apply`.

```bash
# Restow all packages
enstow restow --source ~/dotfiles

# Restow specific packages
enstow restow --source ~/dotfiles zsh nvim
```

### unstow

Removes symlinks pointing into the dotfile repository and removes decrypted plaintext secret targets. Unstow safely verifies symlink targets before removing them to avoid deleting unmanaged files.

```bash
# Unstow all packages
enstow unstow --source ~/dotfiles

# Unstow specific packages
enstow unstow --source ~/dotfiles zsh
```

### status

Audits managed dotfiles, comparing source files against target locations. Reports sync state and detects configuration drift.

```bash
# Human-readable status overview
enstow status

# JSON formatted status output
enstow status --json

# Check status with explicit age key to verify encrypted secrets
enstow status --age-key-file ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt
```

#### Status States Reported

- `SYNCED`: Symlink points to valid source, or decrypted plaintext in destination matches source secret.
- `MISSING`: Source file exists in dotfiles, but target file has not been deployed.
- `CONFLICT`: Target destination contains an unmanaged file, incorrect symlink, or directory blocking deployment.
- `MODIFIED`: Target secret file exists, but plaintext contents have drifted from the encrypted source.
- `UNVERIFIED`: Target secret file exists, but cannot be decrypted for verification due to missing age keys.

### encrypt

Encrypts a plaintext dotfile into `.age` format using specified recipient keys or keys extracted from an age identity file.

```bash
# Encrypt file to explicit recipient
enstow encrypt ~/.config/app/secret.conf \
  --output ~/dotfiles/app/.config/app/secret.conf.age \
  --recipient age1ql3z7hjy54pw3hyww5ayyfg7zqgvc7w3j2elw8zmrj2kg5sfn9aqmcac8p

# Encrypt using identity key file to resolve recipient public key
enstow encrypt ~/.env --age-key-file ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt
```

Options:

- `<file>`: File to encrypt (required).
- `-o, --output <PATH>`: Output encrypted file path (defaults to `<file>.age`).
- `-r, --recipient <KEY>`: Age recipient public key (can be repeated).
- `--age-key-file <PATH>`: Identity file containing private keys to derive public keys.

### edit

Interactively decrypts an age secret file into a secure temporary file, opens it in `$ENSTOW_EDITOR`, `$VISUAL`, `$EDITOR`, or `--editor`, and re-encrypts it upon editor exit if modified.

```bash
# Edit an encrypted dotfile
enstow edit ~/dotfiles/zsh/.zshrc.local.age

# Edit using a specific editor
enstow edit ~/dotfiles/zsh/.zshrc.local.age --editor nvim
```

Options:

- `<file>`: Encrypted age file to edit (required).
- `-r, --recipient <KEY>`: Recipient public key for re-encryption.
- `--age-key-file <PATH>`: Age identity key file for decryption and recipient derivation.
- `--editor <CMD>`: Custom editor executable name or command.

### completions

Outputs shell completion scripts for dynamic or static shell integration.

```bash
# Dynamic completions (recommended)
enstow completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_enstow

# Static completions fallback
enstow completions --static bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/enstow
```

Supported shells:

- `bash`
- `zsh`
- `fish`
- `powershell`
- `elvish`

### man

Generates the UNIX roff format manual page for `enstow` to stdout.

```bash
enstow man > assets/enstow.1
```

---

## Conflict Resolution, Backups & Pruning

### Conflict Detection

Before creating symlinks or writing decrypted files, `enstow` checks the target path:

- If target does not exist: Proceed with creation.
- If target is a symlink pointing to the expected source: Mark `SYNCED` / skip.
- If target is a symlink pointing elsewhere, or a regular file: Flag as `CONFLICT`.

### Resolution Flags

1. `--dry-run` (`-n`): Simulates execution and outputs planned operations without altering filesystem.
2. `--force` (`-f`): Overwrites conflicting target files or recreates differing symlinks.
3. `--backup` (`-b`): Relocates conflicting files into `<backup-dir>` prior to creating new links or secret targets.
4. `--backup-dir <PATH>`: Specifies backup directory (defaults to `<target>/.enstow-backup`). Preserves relative directory hierarchy.
5. `--prune`: During `apply` or `restow`, detects and deletes dangling symlinks in target paths that point to deleted or moved source files.

---

## Secret Management & Encryption

### Detection Patterns & Destination Mapping

`enstow` recognizes secrets by file extension and naming convention, mapping them to plaintext target filenames:

| Source File Pattern | Encryption Engine | Deployed Target Filename | Target Permissions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `<name>.age` | `age` | `<name>` | `0600` (`-rw-------`) |
| `<name>.sops.yaml` | `sops` | `<name>.yaml` | `0600` (`-rw-------`) |
| `<name>.sops.json` | `sops` | `<name>.json` | `0600` (`-rw-------`) |
| `<name>.sops.<ext>` | `sops` | `<name>.<ext>` | `0600` (`-rw-------`) |
| `.sops.yaml` (exact) | `sops` | `.sops.yaml` | `0600` (`-rw-------`) |

Regular non-secret files are linked directly via filesystem symlinks (`symlink(source, target)`).

### Permissions & Memory Safety

- **In-Memory Decryption:** Decryption buffers are held in memory and never written to temporary unencrypted dotfile paths.
- **Strict File Permissions:** Decrypted secret target files are created with mode `0600` (`-rw-------`) on Unix systems to prevent unauthorized access.
- **Cross-Platform Security:** Path traversal attempts and permission setting failures are caught and reported as errors.

### Age Recipient Resolution

When encrypting or re-encrypting via `enstow encrypt` or `enstow edit`:

1. Explicit `--recipient` flags take priority.
2. If omitted, recipients are extracted from `--age-key-file`, `$ENSTOW_AGE_KEY_FILE`, or `$SOPS_AGE_KEY_FILE`.
3. If omitted, recipients configured in `config.toml` (`recipients = [...]`) or environment variable `$ENSTOW_RECIPIENTS` are used.
4. If a private key file is provided, `enstow` derives the public recipient key automatically.

---

## Ignore Rules & Patterns

### Default Ignores

The following files and directories are ignored by default across all packages:

- `.git`
- `.gitignore`
- `.codegraph`
- `.serena`
- `.agents`
- `.github`
- `target`
- `Cargo.lock`
- `.enstowignore`
- `.stow-local-ignore`

### Custom Ignore Files

1. `.enstowignore`: Placed in source root or package directories. Lines starting with `#` and empty lines are ignored.
2. `.stow-local-ignore`: Fallback compatibility format matching GNU stow conventions.
3. Command Line `--ignore <pattern>`: Passed directly via CLI or configuration file.

Patterns match relative file paths using standard glob patterns (e.g. `*.tmp`, `*.swp`, `.DS_Store`).

---

## Configuration & Precedence

### Hierarchical Precedence Order

Configuration settings resolve in strict precedence (highest to lowest):

1. **CLI Flags & Arguments** (`--source`, `--target`, `--force`, `--backup`, etc.)
2. **Environment Variables** (`ENSTOW_SOURCE`, `ENSTOW_TARGET`, etc.)
3. **Configuration File** (`~/.config/enstow/config.toml`, `.yaml`, or `.json`)
4. **Built-in Defaults** (source: `.`, target: `$HOME`, backup_dir: `$target/.enstow-backup`)

### Configuration File Schema

Supported locations:

- `$ENSTOW_CONFIG` (explicit flag or environment variable)
- `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/enstow/config.toml` (or `config.yaml`, `config.json`)
- `~/.config/enstow/config.toml`

#### TOML Example (`~/.config/enstow/config.toml`)

```toml
source = "~/dotfiles"
target = "~"
dry_run = false
force = false
backup = false
backup_dir = "~/.enstow-backup"
prune = true
age_key_file = "~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt"
recipients = [
  "age1ql3z7hjy54pw3hyww5ayyfg7zqgvc7w3j2elw8zmrj2kg5sfn9aqmcac8p"
]
packages = ["zsh", "nvim", "git"]
editor = "nvim"
ignore = ["*.tmp", ".DS_Store", "*.swp"]
json = false
log_level = "info"
```

#### YAML Example (`~/.config/enstow/config.yaml`)

```yaml
source: ~/dotfiles
target: ~
dry_run: false
force: false
backup: false
backup_dir: ~/.enstow-backup
prune: true
age_key_file: ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt
recipients:
  - age1ql3z7hjy54pw3hyww5ayyfg7zqgvc7w3j2elw8zmrj2kg5sfn9aqmcac8p
packages:
  - zsh
  - nvim
  - git
editor: nvim
ignore:
  - "*.tmp"
  - ".DS_Store"
  - "*.swp"
json: false
log_level: info
```

#### JSON Example (`~/.config/enstow/config.json`)

```json
{
  "source": "~/dotfiles",
  "target": "~",
  "dry_run": false,
  "force": false,
  "backup": false,
  "backup_dir": "~/.enstow-backup",
  "prune": true,
  "age_key_file": "~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt",
  "recipients": [
    "age1ql3z7hjy54pw3hyww5ayyfg7zqgvc7w3j2elw8zmrj2kg5sfn9aqmcac8p"
  ],
  "packages": [
    "zsh",
    "nvim",
    "git"
  ],
  "editor": "nvim",
  "ignore": [
    "*.tmp",
    ".DS_Store",
    "*.swp"
  ],
  "json": false,
  "log_level": "info"
}
```

---

## Environment Variables Reference

| Environment Variable | Description | Equivalent Flag / Config |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ENSTOW_CONFIG` | Path to explicit configuration file | `-C, --config` |
| `ENSTOW_SOURCE` | Default dotfiles source directory | `-s, --source` |
| `ENSTOW_TARGET` | Destination directory for dotfiles | `-t, --target` |
| `ENSTOW_DRY_RUN` | Enable dry-run mode (`1`, `true`) | `-n, --dry-run` |
| `ENSTOW_FORCE` | Force overwrite existing files (`1`, `true`) | `-f, --force` |
| `ENSTOW_BACKUP` | Backup conflicting files before overwrite (`1`, `true`) | `-b, --backup` |
| `ENSTOW_BACKUP_DIR` | Directory to relocate backup files | `--backup-dir` |
| `ENSTOW_PRUNE` | Prune stale symlinks on apply (`1`, `true`) | `--prune` |
| `ENSTOW_AGE_KEY_FILE` | Primary path to age private identity keys | `--age-key-file` |
| `SOPS_AGE_KEY_FILE` | Fallback path to age private identity keys | `--age-key-file` |
| `ENSTOW_RECIPIENTS` | Comma-separated list of age recipient public keys | `-r, --recipient` |
| `SOPS_AGE_RECIPIENTS` | Fallback comma-separated recipient keys | `-r, --recipient` |
| `ENSTOW_PACKAGES` | Comma-separated list of default packages | `[PACKAGES...]` |
| `ENSTOW_EDITOR` | Editor for secret modification in `enstow edit` | `--editor` |
| `VISUAL` / `EDITOR` | Standard fallback editors for `enstow edit` | `--editor` |
| `ENSTOW_IGNORE` | Comma-separated glob patterns to ignore | `-i, --ignore` |
| `ENSTOW_JSON` | Enable JSON output for status command (`1`, `true`) | `--json` |
| `ENSTOW_LOG_LEVEL` | Log level (`trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`) | `--log-level` |
| `RUST_LOG` | Tracing filter directive | `--log-level` |

---

## Core Rust Modules & Internal Architecture

### `src/lib.rs`

Declares public library modules:

- `pub mod cli;`
- `pub mod config;`
- `pub mod crypto;`
- `pub mod error;`
- `pub mod stow;`

### `src/cli.rs`

Handles argument parsing and completions:

- `struct Cli`: Root parser with global options (`config`, `log_level`, `verbose`, `quiet`), subcommands, and common arguments.
- `struct CommonArgs`: Shared arguments across stow/unstow/restow/status. Resolves `source_path()`, `target_path()`, and `backup_dir_path()`.
- `enum Commands`: Subcommands enum (`Apply`, `Restow`, `Unstow`, `Encrypt`, `Edit`, `Status`, `Man`, `Completions`).
- `fn generate_manpage(...)`: Renders man page using `clap_mangen`.
- `fn generate_completions(...)`: Dynamic environment completer with static fallback via `clap_complete`.

### `src/stow.rs`

Implements filesystem scanning and planning:

- `enum FileAction`: Represents planned filesystem mutation:
  - `Link { source: PathBuf, target: PathBuf }`: Create regular symlink.
  - `DecryptSecret { source: PathBuf, target: PathBuf, secret_type: SecretType }`: In-memory decryption and 0600 target write.
  - `Unlink { target: PathBuf }`: Remove managed symlink.
  - `RemoveSecret { target: PathBuf }`: Remove managed secret file.
- `enum EntryStatus`: Status classification (`Synced`, `Missing`, `Conflict`, `Modified`, `Unverified`).
- `struct FileActionStatus`: Pairs `FileAction` with evaluated `EntryStatus` and message.
- `fn plan_stow(args: &CommonArgs) -> Result<Vec<FileAction>, EnstowError>`: Scans package directories, applies ignore filters, and computes destination actions.
- `fn plan_unstow(args: &CommonArgs) -> Result<Vec<FileAction>, EnstowError>`: Scans destination directories to locate managed symlinks and secret files for removal.
- `fn plan_prune(args: &CommonArgs) -> Result<Vec<FileAction>, EnstowError>`: Locates stale symlinks in destination pointing to deleted source paths.
- `fn execute_plan(...)`: Performs atomic linking, writing, and directory creation.
- `fn execute_plan_with_backup(...)`: Moves conflicting files to backup path before applying changes.
- `fn check_status(...)`: Compares planned source actions against target filesystem state to produce status entries.

### `src/crypto.rs`

Handles cryptographic operations:

- `enum SecretType`: Categorizes secrets (`Age`, `Sops`).
- `fn detect_secret_type(path: &Path) -> Option<SecretType>`: Identifies secret file type based on extension.
- `fn target_plaintext_name(path: &Path) -> Option<String>`: Translates encrypted filename to plaintext equivalent.
- `fn decrypt_to_memory(...) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EnstowError>`: Decrypts file in memory without writing temporary files.
- `fn decrypt_age(path: &Path, key_file: Option<&Path>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EnstowError>`: Age decryption supporting armored and binary formats, identity keys, and passphrase prompting.
- `fn decrypt_sops(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EnstowError>`: SOPS decryption via `sops --decrypt` execution.
- `fn encrypt_file_age(...) -> Result<(), EnstowError>`: Encrypts file to age recipients.
- `fn write_secure_file(path: &Path, content: &[u8], force: bool) -> Result<(), EnstowError>`: Writes decrypted buffer to disk with permissions `0600`.
- `fn edit_file_age(...) -> Result<(), EnstowError>`: Decrypts secret to secure temporary file, launches editor, and re-encrypts if content changed.

### `src/config.rs`

Parses configuration files:

- `enum ConfigFormat`: `Toml`, `Yaml`, `Json` derived from file extension.
- `struct ConfigFile`: Serde-deserializable configuration representation.
- `fn load_config(...) -> Result<ConfigFile, EnstowError>`: Searches configuration paths and parses appropriate format.
- `fn merge_args(...)`: Merges configuration file settings into CLI arguments with CLI precedence.

### `src/error.rs`

Structured domain errors using `thiserror`:

- `enum EnstowError`:
  - `Io { path: PathBuf, source: std::io::Error }`
  - `Decryption { path: PathBuf, message: String }`
  - `Encryption { path: PathBuf, message: String }`
  - `Conflict { path: PathBuf, message: String }`
  - `Config(String)`
  - `NotFound(PathBuf)`

### `src/main.rs`

Executable orchestration:

- Sets up `tracing_subscriber` with environment and flag filtering.
- Reads configuration and merges with CLI parameters.
- Dispatches execution to command handlers.
- Formats errors cleanly and exits with appropriate exit codes.

---

## Development, Testing & Quality Gates

The project uses `task` (`go-task`) for workflow automation.

### Available Tasks

```bash
# Run all tests, formatting, and linting
task test

# Format code with rustfmt
task fmt

# Check formatting without modifying files
task fmt:check

# Format Markdown documentation with rumdl
task fmt:md

# Lint code with clippy (-D warnings)
task lint

# Lint Markdown files with rumdl
task lint:md

# Run cargo check
task check

# Run unit and integration tests
cargo test

# Generate UNIX roff man page
task man

# Generate shell completion files
task completions

# Run test coverage report
task coverage

# Cross-compile release binaries for all targets (x86_64, aarch64, armv7, armv6)
task build

# Build locally in release mode
task build:local
```

### CI Verification Matrix

GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs quality checks across multiple platforms:

- Linux (`ubuntu-latest`), macOS (`macos-latest`), Windows (`windows-latest`)
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --all-targets --all-features`
- `rumdl check .` (Markdown linting)
- `taplo lint` & `taplo fmt --check` (TOML validation)
- Code coverage via `cargo-llvm-cov` uploaded to Coveralls
